references.text: The original oath that the leaders of Israel swore to the Gibeonites, which they must now keep to avoid God's wrath
The context in which the people grumbled against the leaders about the oath, but the leaders insisted on keeping it
The law that an oath to the Lord must be kept and not broken
The importance of keeping promises made to God, to avoid His wrath
The consequences of Saul breaking the oath with the Gibeonites, which led to a famine in Israel
Zedekiah's breach of the oath to the king of Babylon led to God's wrath and judgment
